subject: gargoyle
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: cathedral gargoyle crouched on a ledge.
Style: gothic stone carving.
reasoning:
I'm planning a compact but detailed gargoyle module, with a crouched stone gargoyle resting on a simple ledge slab whose base sits at y=0, built using the agentic-3js-builder API with a default export and meta export.

I'm working out the skeleton: hip, spine chain, neck, head, and tail joints positioned to form a crouched pose facing forward, plus stone paint logic combining a mottled grey base with a noise-based moss overlay on upward-facing surfaces, and defining the spine joint chain with named segments leading up to the chest.

Now I'm continuing the joint hierarchy, adding the neck chain, a separate head joint aimed forward-down, and a jaw joint attached to the head, then starting the body sweep that will use these bones to shape the torso mesh.

Adding a chest bulk sphere for heavy build, then shaping the head with a blocky skull box, a tapered muzzle frustum, and a separate lower jaw piece.

For details, I'm adding small cone teeth, a brow ridge box, and eye sockets carved dark with glowing orange pupils for that gothic stone look. Horns sweep out from the skull using a bezier curve, ears get pointed extrusions, and nostrils are tiny dark spheres -- all positioned using head-local directional coordinates where I need to keep track of which way is model-right versus world orientation.

Now I'm designing folded bat wings rising from the shoulders, using extrusion along an outward-and-back axis with a scalloped wing outline defined by a series of coordinate points to get that classic bat-wing silhouette.

Since gargoyle wings should be extended rather than folded, I'm angling the wing direction outward and tilted. I'm adding bone rods running from the shoulder root out to each wing tip using the wing's local coordinate frame, and setting up a shoulder joint to connect the wing to the chest for proper articulation.

Defining the wing chain for each side using a mirrored x-offset, with root/wrist/tip points sketched out for the shoulder-to-wingtip path.

I'm estimating the overall gargoyle height by stacking the wing extent above the shoulder plus the ledge height.

That's too tall compared to the body, so I'm scaling the whole outline down by roughly 0.65, which brings the wing span and total height into proportion. Then I'm positioning the crouched hind legs with hips set back and feet planted on the ledge, using a limb function with bend parameters to pose them.

Working out the crouched leg geometry: hip, knee, and ankle joints with forward-up bend directions, and tapering radii for the thigh and shin segments...

For the foot, I'm adding three toe capsules spreading outward with small claw spikes at the tips, setting the foot height so toes sink slightly into the ground. Now I'm moving on to the arms, positioning the shoulder joint and planning the hand target.

Positioning the hand on the ledge edge, I'm working out the arm geometry—computing distances and bend angles so the crouched pose has elbows splayed outward and up, with three forward-facing claws on the fingers. Then I'm starting the tail, building a curved chain of points sweeping down and back from the hips.

I'm reworking the ledge to be deeper so the tail can curl and rest on its surface instead of hanging off the edge, adjusting the tail's control points to curl sideways with a tapering radius, and planning a small spade-like arrowhead extrusion for the tip.

Now I'm adding spiky dorsal ridge details swept along the spine with stone coloring, and considering extra surface ornamentation like a carved inscription plaque or quatrefoil decoration on the ledge's front face.

For the ledge itself, I'm building a base slab with a wider cornice on top and dentil-like teeth along the front edge using looped box parts, keeping the whole structure's bottom anchored at y=0. I'll texture the ledge front with a quatrefoil pattern and moss paint patches, then add glowing ember eyes set into dark sockets using the glow kit.

I'm also thinking through stone color layering -- a mottled base tone with mossy patches blended in based on surface normal and noise thresholds, plus considering a countershading pass for the darker underside.

For the overall stone material I'm countershading the mossy base against a darker mottled tone to add shadow depth, and noting I can rely on paint/noise/mix/smoothstep helpers from the SDK. I'll make a separate ledge stone variant with heavier grime and moss via a reusable makeStone(seed, mossAmt) function, skip the vein detail for wings in favor of calling makeStone directly, and start blocking out the eye sockets with a dark sphere plus a glowing inner sphere.

Now I'm positioning the glowing eye, sizing the brow wedge, and placing it with rotation adjustments to angle the slope correctly relative to the head's forward direction. I'm also sketching the skull box dimensions and the muzzle as a tapered frustum shape running from the head forward to the nose, working out how width and height map onto the local axes so the taper looks right.

Now I'm adding the nose bump and nostril spheres, then building the lower jaw as another tapered frustum anchored to a jaw joint offset below and forward of the head. I'm placing upper fangs on the head bone and lower fangs on the jaw bone as small cone spikes, then setting up a loop to add a few smaller teeth along each side of the jaw row.

I'm positioning the jaw pivot point and sizing the lower jaw box so its top edge aligns just below the muzzle, then working out the head's placement at the end of the neck path with a slight downward tilt for a hunched, glaring posture. Now I'm sketching the curved horns sweeping back from the skull using a bezier path on each side.

Finalizing the ear outline shape, then adding a bulky chest sphere scaled and positioned relative to the chest bone joint.

Now I'm placing haunch spheres near the hips and shoulders, then reworking the spine curve between hips and chest. I'm realizing the hips sit too low relative to the belly ledge, so I'm lowering the hip and chest heights for a more crouched posture before working out leg and foot positions.

For the legs I'm computing bone lengths needed to fold sharply from hip to foot, settling on shorter segments for a tucked stance. For the arms I'm measuring shoulder-to-hand distance and choosing bend lengths and direction so the elbow juts outward and slightly forward, keeping the shoulder joint offset from the midline for a natural gargoyle pose.

Now I'm mapping out the spine chain from pelvis to chest to neck to head, making sure the head sits forward and the top of the skull plus wingspan stay within the overall model height including the ledge. I'm also settling joint naming conventions for each limb chain -- shoulder/elbow/wrist for arms, hip/knee/ankle for legs -- and renaming the wing joints to wingRoot/wingWrist/wingTip to avoid clashing with the arm joint names.

Writing claw geometry...

Skipping wing joint posing for now, and planning to add rib lines on the wing membrane using thin rods anchored at the wing root, scaled along the outline with a slight thickness offset.

For the ribs, I'll keep rods centered at z=0 with radius 0.014 so they protrude slightly above the thinner 0.02 slab, creating raised ridges. For orientation, I'm defining the wing's local x and y axes so it extends outward and slightly back, considering a small inward lean at the top for a more natural silhouette.

Now I'm working out the wing joint chain as a polyline from the root through approximate wrist and tip positions, extruded along that bone path. For the ledge, I'm adding a quatrefoil texture using a simple SVG of four overlapping circles in a muted grey tone, placed on the front face of the ledge's base box.

Adding 13 small dentil boxes under the cornice along the front face. I'm skipping corner pinnacles, but giving the gargoyle a slightly open jaw pose to act as a waterspout, plus planning a stone gutter trough across the back to channel rain.

For surface detail I'm sticking with spine ridge, brow, cheek spikes, chin goatee spike, and shoulder/knee spikes, and adding cracks via a cell-noise paint function that darkens narrow cell boundaries. Writing the stone paint function...

Building the body sweep and dorsal spikes along the spine, then starting on the haunch geometry for the hind legs...

Still writing joint hierarchy...

Finalizing the outline now, ready to produce the full output.
